title: Static vs Dynamic Routing: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: You can navigate with a paper map. Or you can use a G P S that updates itself. Routers have the same choice.

scenes.heading: Road map vs GPS
scenes.narration: A delivery driver needs a way to find customers. A paper map is static routing, and you write each route yourself. A G P S is dynamic routing, which updates when roads close. The map costs nothing to run, and nobody can mess with it. The G P S reacts faster when something breaks.

scenes.heading: Comparison
scenes.narration: Pick the right tool. Static is manual, and dynamic is automatic. Static suits small stable networks, and dynamic suits large ones. Dynamic uses some bandwidth and processing.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Dynamic isn't always better. A static route needs a reachable next hop. And distance and metric are different things.

items.right: Static wins for small stable sites
The next hop must be reachable

items.wrong: AD and metric are the same
items.right: AD compares sources; metric compares paths
